analysis.subject: finance
analysis.pageCoverage: Page explains loan interest rate as borrowing cost, APR as rate plus lender fees like origination charges, federal disclosure of APR under TILA, using APR to compare auto loans, and how credit score and shopping affect rates.

overview.headline: How interest rate and APR measure loan cost and allow comparison

keyPoints.point: An interest rate is the cost you pay to the lender for borrowing money on top of principal.
keyPoints.quote: An interest rate is the cost you pay to the lender for borrowing money to finance your loan, on top of the loan amount or your principal.

keyPoints.point: APR equals the interest rate plus additional fees charged by the lender such as origination charges.
keyPoints.quote: The APR is the interest rate plus any additional fees charged by the lender.

keyPoints.point: Federal law requires lenders to disclose APR and other important loan terms before you finalize your car loan.
keyPoints.quote: The federal Truth in Lending Act (TILA) requires lenders to give you specific disclosures about the important terms in your loan, including the APR.

keyPoints.point: You can compare APRs to APRs across lenders to shop for the best loan costs.
keyPoints.quote: Since all lenders must provide the APR, you can use the APR to compare auto loans.

keyPoints.point: Higher credit scores generally lead to lower rates, but shopping around helps reduce costs.
keyPoints.quote: In general, the higher your credit score, the lower your rates will be.

keyTerms.gloss: cost paid to the lender for borrowing money to finance the loan
keyTerms.quote: An interest rate is the cost you pay to the lender for borrowing money to finance your loan, on top of the loan amount or your principal.

keyTerms.gloss: measure that adds additional fees to the interest rate
keyTerms.quote: The APR is the interest rate plus any additional fees charged by the lender.

keyTerms.gloss: loan amount on top of which borrowing cost is charged
keyTerms.quote: An interest rate is the cost you pay to the lender for borrowing money to finance your loan, on top of the loan amount or your principal.

keyTerms.gloss: fees charged when the loan is made by the lender
keyTerms.quote: This includes origination charges and other fees charged when the loan is made.

keyTerms.gloss: rating that helps determine the rates lenders offer a borrower
keyTerms.quote: In general, the higher your credit score, the lower your rates will be.

keyTerms.gloss: specific information lenders must give about important loan terms
keyTerms.quote: The federal Truth in Lending Act (TILA) requires lenders to give you specific disclosures about the important terms in your loan, including the APR.
